items.label: TE_STATE_NONRESIDENT_FLAT_RATE
items.detail: AR nonresident tax is an effective-rate estimate; most states compute nonresident tax by ratio of the full return (AR method: ratio).

items.label: TE_STATE_CREDIT_RESIDENT_SIDE
items.detail: MO: the credit for taxes paid to other states is taken on the resident return. Reverse-credit pairs (AZ, CA, OR, VA, IN and DC with each other) grant it on the NONRESIDENT return instead — not modelled; the estimate may differ.

items.label: TE_SCH_AI_ASSUMPTION
items.detail: Q13a: the §199A deduction in each Schedule AI column is figured on the annualized amounts (Schedule AI line 9).

items.label: TE_SCH_AI_ASSUMPTION
items.detail: Q13b: credits in each column are the FULL-YEAR credits, not annualized (Schedule AI line 19); the standard deduction is the full-year amount (line 7).

items.label: TE_SCH_AI_ASSUMPTION
items.detail: The deductible part of SE tax in each column follows the engine's SE tax on the annualized inputs; it equals Part II when the factor is 12 ÷ months.

items.label: TE_SCH_AI_ASSUMPTION
items.detail: Itemized deductions, HSA, retirement deferrals and Schedule 1-A amounts are annualized with the income (Schedule AI line 4); UBIA is not. Self-employed health insurance in a column is the period's premiums for the months deductible within the period, annualized.

items.label: TE_STATE_NO_ANNUALIZATION
items.detail: MO: installments use the regular method only; annualized-income installments (the state's Schedule AI equivalent, where it allows one) are not computed, so a federal Schedule AI reduction does not carry to the state vouchers.

items.label: TE_ESTIMATES_NOT_REQUIRED
items.detail: AR: estimates are not required (required when the tax is more than $1,000).

items.label: Age thresholds
items.detail: Age-based amounts (65 / 50 / 55 / 60–63) come from parameters that are still awaiting verification.

items.label: SIMPLE catch-up
items.detail: The SIMPLE IRA age 60–63 super catch-up is not applied.

items.label: Itemized limits
items.detail: The charitable 60%-of-AGI limit and the mortgage-interest debt limits are not applied.

items.label: MAGI
items.detail: Modified AGI is taken as AGI for the SALT phase-down, Schedule 1-A and the §469(i) allowance.

items.label: Car-loan interest
items.detail: The Schedule 1-A car-loan interest phase-out is applied linearly.

items.label: Self-employed health insurance
items.detail: For an S corporation shareholder the SEHI cap is the officer wages; the cap is pooled across businesses.

items.label: Owner items
items.detail: Owner-level items (health insurance, retirement) are run-rated as recurring; items not tied to a person go to the primary taxpayer.

items.label: QBI minimum
items.detail: The §199A(i) minimum deduction is applied after the overall limitation.

items.label: Passive / excess business loss
items.detail: §469(i) MAGI is AGI without passive losses; the §461(l) aggregate is ordinary + rental + §1231 of non-investment activities plus guaranteed payments after §469.

items.label: NIIT
items.detail: Gains are treated as net investment income without a trade-or-business carve-out.

items.label: Prior-year return
items.detail: A prior-year overpayment is credited on the original due date; a late-filed prior return is not modelled.

items.label: Penalty method
items.detail: Underpayment penalties are figured per Form 2210 / state worksheets with periods split at rate changes; actual assessments may differ.

items.label: Disclaimer
items.detail: Projection based on bookkeeping records and the assumptions listed. Not a tax return.
